report.summary: All four failures are one timing problem, not a product regression: the app's list_books() sleeps a random 0-8 seconds on every /books render, and the UI tests give the page only 5 seconds. Fix the app's random delay first (app/main.py:150), then the 5-second UI timeout in tests/ui/conftest.py:7 is only a secondary concern.

causes.title: App randomly delays /books rendering by up to 8 s, exceeding the 5 s UI timeout
causes.explanation: list_books() calls time.sleep(random.uniform(0, 8)) before querying the database. render_books() calls list_books() for every /books page render, and the post-register redirect lands on /books. The UI fixture sets a 5000 ms default timeout (tests/ui/conftest.py:7). Whenever the random sleep draws more than about 5 s, page.goto('/books') or the register click's navigation wait times out. Roughly 3 in 8 renders should exceed the limit, so the same code can pass on a rerun. The app is only sometimes slow, so per the triage rules this is flaky, not a product_bug. The three goto timeouts and the Register click timeout all come from this one delay. The click failure's call log ends at 'waiting for scheduled navigations to finish', which is the redirect to /books being held by this sleep. The failure text does not prove this directly, but the code path makes it the most likely cause.
evidence: tests/ui/conftest.py:6 docstring: "Nothing in this app should take longer than 5 s"
tests/ui/test_login_ui.py:9: AuthPage(page).open_register().submit(...)  -> Locator.click: Timeout 5000ms exceeded. ... waiting for scheduled navigations to finish
Failure call log for test_added_book_is_listed: navigating to "http://127.0.0.1:63061/books", waiting until "load" (Timeout 5000ms)
Failure call log for test_book_created_through_api_shows_in_ui and test_future_year_shows_error_and_keeps_input: same goto /books timeout
causes.suggested_fix: Remove the random sleep from list_books() in app/main.py:150, or make any simulated latency deterministic and opt-in (for example, behind an environment variable that only a dedicated slow-path test enables). Do not raise the 5 s limit to paper over it. If the team wants to keep a latency simulation, the tests should wait on a specific element, not on the load event. Then rerun the ui suite several times to confirm the failures are gone.
